title: Profiling of hypoxic and extracellular matrix remodeling markers in biofluids and cerebral tissue after traumatic brain injury: expression and signaling crosstalk of HIF-1alpha, MMP-9/14 and EPHA2.
authors: Poniatowski, Lukasz A; Olczak, Mieszko; Acewicz, Albert; Kwiatkowska, Magdalena; Siwinska, Agnieszka
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过免疫组化和ELISA检测TBI患者脑组织和体液中HIF-1alpha、MMP-9/14及EPHA2的表达，属于纯湿实验生物标志物分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a formidable clinical, neuropathological, and forensic challenge, constituting a leading cause of death as well a neuroscientific research target worldwide. A deeper understanding of the molecular signatures underlying vascular and extracellular matrix remodeling in TBI seems to be critical both for the development of diagnostic biomarkers in post-mortem neuropathology and for identifying potential therapeutic targets in the acute injury setting. Despite the individual exploration of HIF-1alpha, MMP-9/14, and EPHA2 in neurological injury, few studies have offered a comprehensive, integrative examination of these biomarkers within the human TBI brain, especially in post-mortem forensic contexts. The study concerned a total of 40 individuals, cases with head injuries (n = 20) suspected to be the cause of death, and atraumatic control cases of sudden death (n = 20) due to cardiopulmonary reasons. Brain tissue was obtained during forensic autopsies and subjected to immunohistochemical staining. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum were collected approximately 24 h post-mortem and analyzed through ELISA testing. We observed the elevated concentration level of HIF-1alpha, MMP-9 and MMP-14 in CSF. In the frontal cortex, anti-EPHA2 immunohistostaining revealed a generalized homogenization of the reaction was observed both within the neuronal bodies (including nuclear area) and their axons among the study group. Rather than relying solely on macroscopic signs of trauma, the present study proposes a layered biomarker architecture wherein HIF-1alpha reflects hypoxic load, MMP-9/14 denotes matrix remodeling and barrier disruption, and EPHA2 signals cellular stress and neurovascular dysregulation. Such a composite signature provides a biological foundation that may ultimately be translated into post-mortem diagnostic algorithms or pilot machine-learning-based forensic stratification tools following validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.
abstract_zh: 创伤性脑损伤（TBI）仍是临床、神经病理学及法医学领域的一项严峻挑战，构成全球范围内死亡的主要原因之一，同时也是神经科学研究的重要靶点。深入理解TBI中血管和细胞外基质重塑背后的分子特征，对于死后神经病理学中诊断生物标志物的开发以及急性损伤情境下潜在治疗靶点的识别均至关重要。尽管HIF-1α、MMP-9/14和EPHA2在神经损伤中已被分别探索，但很少有研究在人类TBI脑组织中，尤其是在死后法医学背景下，对这些生物标志物进行综合性、整合性的检验。本研究共涉及40例个体，包括疑似因头部损伤（n=20）致死的病例，以及因心肺原因猝死的非创伤性对照病例（n=20）。脑组织在法医尸检中获取，并进行免疫组织化学染色。脑脊液（CSF）和血清在死后约24小时收集，并通过ELISA检测分析。我们观察到CSF中HIF-1α、MMP-9和MMP-14的浓度水平升高。在额叶皮层中，抗EPHA2免疫组化染色显示，研究组内神经元胞体（包括核区域）及其轴突中均观察到反应的普遍均质化。本研究并非仅依赖创伤的宏观体征，而是提出了一种分层生物标志物架构，其中HIF-1α反映缺氧负荷，MMP-9/14指示基质重塑和屏障破坏，EPHA2则标志细胞应激和神经血管失调。这种复合特征提供了生物学基础，在更大规模的多中心队列中验证后，最终可能转化为死后诊断算法或基于机器学习的法医学分层试点工具。
